content.value_statement: Weak prompts create inconsistent LLM behavior, higher token costs, and difficult testing. This skill turns rough instructions into structured prompts with evaluation, safety, and deployment guidance.
actual_capabilities: Reviews existing prompts for clarity, structure, ambiguity, and performance risks.
Applies reasoning, few-shot, self-critique, and model-specific prompt patterns.
Designs prompts for GPT, Claude, Gemini, RAG, support, analysis, and code tasks.
Creates testing protocols with typical, edge, adversarial, and out-of-scope cases.
Suggests deployment practices for versioning, rollout, monitoring, and iteration.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates, not a running prompt evaluation service.
Performance claims still need validation against your own models and data.
It does not replace security review for prompts used in high-risk workflows.
It may need domain examples from you for specialized tasks.

use_cases.title: Improve Product Prompts
use_cases.description: Convert rough feature prompts into structured instructions with objectives, examples, output formats, and quality checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare LLM App Prompts
use_cases.description: Build production prompts for support, data analysis, RAG, and code generation workflows.

use_cases.title: Standardize Prompt Testing
use_cases.description: Create evaluation plans with edge cases, adversarial cases, scoring criteria, and deployment monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Prompt Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single draft prompt.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt for clarity, missing context, ambiguity, and output format issues. Then provide a stronger version and explain the changes. Prompt: {prompt}

prompt_templates.title: Model-Specific Rewrite
prompt_templates.scenario: Adapt one prompt for a target model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Optimize this prompt for {model}. Preserve the task goal, add clear sections, improve instruction order, and recommend parameters. Prompt: {prompt}

prompt_templates.title: Few-Shot Production Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a prompt that includes examples and constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production prompt for {task}. Include role, context, steps, constraints, output format, three examples, error handling, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Prompt System Evaluation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced testing plan for an LLM workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an evaluation plan for this LLM workflow: {workflow}. Include test categories, scoring rubric, safety checks, rollout plan, monitoring metrics, and iteration rules.

output_examples.input: A short support prompt that says, "Answer customer questions about our product."
output_examples.output: An improved support prompt with role, product context, diagnostic steps, escalation rules, response length limits, and a clear response format.

output_examples.input: A data analysis prompt without validation steps or confidence reporting.
output_examples.output: A structured analyst prompt with data checks, trend analysis, segment review, confidence levels, recommendations, and testing guidance.

output_examples.input: A team wants to deploy a new RAG prompt into production.
output_examples.output: A prompt package with source-use instructions, citation rules, gap handling, evaluation cases, rollout stages, and monitoring metrics.

best_practices: Start with the task goal, constraints, required inputs, and exact output format.
Test prompts with normal, edge, adversarial, and out-of-scope examples before deployment.
Track prompt versions, model settings, success rates, cost, latency, and user feedback.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on vague instructions like "be helpful" for production workflows.
Do not add reasoning steps when a concise deterministic answer is enough.
Do not assume one optimized prompt will perform equally across all models.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize?
faq.answer: It optimizes LLM prompts for clarity, structure, reasoning, examples, safety, evaluation, and deployment readiness.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, and the playbook includes model-specific guidance.

faq.question: Can it create prompts for RAG systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a RAG pattern with document context, relevance checks, synthesis rules, citations, and gap reporting.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It designs test cases, rubrics, and monitoring plans, but you must run evaluations in your own environment.

faq.question: Is it only for developers?
faq.answer: No. Developers, product managers, support teams, analysts, and AI quality teams can use the guidance.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the current prompt, target model, task goal, sample inputs, desired output format, constraints, and success criteria.
